comments.body:
Root cause confirmed and fix pushed as Gerrit 3259 (patch set 1, 3b00a2350ba94fdccc176d91ab8ce1c715453d7b).

Reproduced in a sandbox store before the fix: a bug linked caused_by a valid origin, closed with caused_by=<origin's first quad> while a second ticket shared that quad. The close succeeded and the edge became caused_by -> '<quad>'. An unknown id gave the same result.

Fix: transition_compute calls the new resolve_explicit_caused_by before any write. A non-blank close --caused-by that does not resolve to exactly 1 ticket raises CommandError (exit 1) naming the candidates, and nothing is written. _resolve_caused_by_culprit no longer falls back to the raw value.

Evidence, worktree fix-herring with .venv/bin first on PATH:
- tests/unit/test_caused_by_unresolved_herring.py: 4 of 5 failed before the fix (2 DID NOT RAISE, missing function, raw '51b0' returned); the unique-short-id control passed. All 5 pass after.
- The 4 existing caused_by/close modules plus the new one: 52 passed.
- Every test module that mentions caused_by, transition_compute, or close_ticket (38 modules, -m 'not integration and not external'): 852 passed, 1 skipped, exit 0.
- make lint exit 0; make typecheck exit 0 (753 source files).

import_ndjson.py also calls transition_compute but passes no caused_by, so the blank short-circuit leaves imports unchanged (covered by test_blank_caused_by_is_not_validated).

Discovered and filed: primitive-flowered-panther, the close path skips the no-referencing-commit refusal that rebar link enforces.

compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem

Ticket frank-rocky-rat (d52f-823f-894e-499a) carries a `caused_by` LINK event (uuid ceae9de7-8992-47c2-855c-60825331adc3, provenance `explicit`) whose `target_id` is the literal string `6ed2`. That quad matches 2 tickets (6ed2-1e12-0780-4efd, 6ed2-24e5-6985-4faa), so the edge points at no ticket. The escaped-defect metrics read it as a proven attribution to a ticket that does not exist.

Reproduced in a sandbox store (temp git repo + `rebar.init_repo`, the fixture pattern in `tests/unit/test_caused_by_dedup_10d0.py`): a bug linked `caused_by` a valid origin, then closed with `caused_by=<origin's first quad>` while a second ticket dir shares that quad. The close succeeds and the valid edge is replaced by `caused_by -> '<quad>'`. An unknown id (`ffff-0000-not-real`) gives the same result.

Root cause, two parts:
1. `_resolve_caused_by_culprit` (`src/rebar/_commands/transition_close.py:269`) returns `resolve_ticket_id(...) or caused_by.strip()` (line 284), so an unresolved value becomes the edge target.
2. `_apply_caused_by` (line 292) runs only AFTER the status commit (call at line 646) and is best-effort, so it cannot refuse. It removes the existing edges (line 318) before writing the raw target.

Precedent for refusing: `link_core` (`src/rebar/_commands/link_revert.py:197-199`) raises `CommandError("Error: ticket '<x>' does not exist")` on an unresolved target before any write. `resolve_ticket_dir_name` (`src/rebar/_ids.py:605`, docstring line 613) calls the `resolve_ticket_id(id) or id` idiom unsafe.

## Approach

Validate an explicit `--caused-by` before the close writes anything, on the one path all 3 surfaces share. CLI (`transition_cli`), library (`src/rebar/_lib_writes.py`), and MCP all call `transition_compute` (`src/rebar/_commands/transition.py:184`), which calls `close_ticket` (line 291).

- Add `resolve_explicit_caused_by(caused_by, target_status, tracker) -> str` to `transition_close.py`. It returns `""` when the target is not `closed` or the value is blank. Otherwise it returns the canonical id from `resolve_ticket_id(value, tracker, quiet=True)`. When that is `None`, it raises `CommandError` (returncode 1). For more than 1 match the message names every candidate. For 0 matches it says no ticket matches. Both messages say that nothing was written. Candidates come from `build_resolver_scan_index` (`src/rebar/_ids.py:286`): the value's alias matches, plus the `sorted_dir_names` entries that start with the value.
- In `transition_compute`, call it once, unconditionally, after the ghost and init checks and before the parent cascade and `close_ticket`. Pass the canonical id on as `caused_by`. A single unconditional assignment adds no branch to `transition_compute`, so its complexity ceiling does not change.
- In `_resolve_caused_by_culprit`, drop the `or caused_by.strip()` fallback and resolve with `quiet=True`. An unresolved explicit value then returns `None`, and the existing early return in `_apply_caused_by` leaves every existing edge in place. This covers any direct caller of `close_ticket`. Fix its docstring, which says an explicit value "always resolves".

The refusal applies to any close given a non-blank `--caused-by`, because the value is an operator statement and a bad one is a typo. A blank flag keeps the blame-derivation path unchanged.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_commands/transition_close.py`: new `resolve_explicit_caused_by`, plus the `_resolve_caused_by_culprit` fallback removal. About 30 lines, so the file stays under the 800-line cap (currently 733).
- `src/rebar/_commands/transition.py`: 1 call in `transition_compute`.
- `tests/unit/test_caused_by_unresolved_herring.py` (new): regression tests.

## Testing

Tests are written first and fail on current `main`. They use the 10d0 sandbox fixture. Each case makes a 4-hex quad ambiguous by creating a second ticket dir that shares the origin's quad.
- Ambiguous 4-hex `caused_by`: `rebar.transition` raises; the message names both candidate ids; the bug is still `in_progress`; the original `caused_by` edge (same `link_uuid`) is the only one.
- Unknown id: same refusal, and the message says no ticket matches.
- Happy path: a unique short id (8-hex two-quad) resolves; after close the edge target is the canonical full id.
- Defense in depth: `_resolve_caused_by_culprit` returns `None` for an ambiguous explicit value.
- Regression: `tests/unit/test_caused_by_dedup_10d0.py`, `tests/unit/test_caused_by_provenance.py`, `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_caused_by_autoderive.py`, and `tests/unit/test_transition_close.py` still pass.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] A close with a `--caused-by` that does not resolve to exactly 1 ticket is refused before any write, with a visible error naming the candidates. It writes no `caused_by` edge, leaves existing edges and status unchanged, and exits 1. Checked by `pytest tests/unit/test_caused_by_unresolved_herring.py`, which drives an ambiguous 4-hex value and an unknown id.
- [x] A uniquely resolving short `--caused-by` records the canonical full id. Checked by the happy-path test in the same module.
- [x] [non-codebase] `make lint` and `make typecheck` exit 0 with the worktree `.venv/bin` first on PATH, and the 4 existing caused_by/close test modules listed under Testing pass. The run results and exit codes are recorded as a ticket comment, and the Gerrit change reaches `Verified +1`.
      provenance: environment=local fix-herring worktree at the change's commit; principal=the operator's local user; privilege_posture=production-equivalent; instrument=live-call — the same make targets and pytest that CI's Verified job runs
- [x] [non-codebase] The dangling `caused_by` edge on frank-rocky-rat is either corrected to the evidenced `6ed2` ticket's full id, with a comment giving the reasoning, or left in place with an evidence comment and reported to the operator as a decision. Checked by `rebar show frank-rocky-rat` and that comment.
      provenance: environment=live rebar tracker (origin tickets branch); principal=the rebar CLI under the configured git identity; privilege_posture=production-equivalent; instrument=live-call — supported rebar link/unlink/comment commands, no raw git
